49330.subject: Chemistry
49330.question_text: Calculate the mass of copper deposited if a current of 0.45A flows through \(CuSO_{4}\) solution for 1hour 15mins.   [Cu=64.0, S= 32.0, O =16.0, 1F= 96500C]
49330.explanation:
\(Cu^{2+} + 2e^{-}  \to  Cu_{(s)}\)

\( 2 \times 96500C = 193000C  deposits 64g of Cu\)

\(M \propto It\)

\(Q = It = 0.45A \times 1hr15mins\)

= \( 0.45 \times 75 \times 60\) [converting the time to seconds]

Quantity of electricity passed = 2025C

\(193000C \to 64g Cu\)

\(1C \to \frac{64}{193000}\)

\(2025C \to \frac{64}{193000} \times 2025\)

\(= 0.6715g  \approxeq  0.67g\)

49342.subject: Chemistry
49342.question_text: A primary alkanol has a molecular mass of 60. What is the structural formula of the compound? [C= 12.0, H= 1.0, O= 16.0)
49342.explanation:
Alkanols have the formula \(C_{n}H_{2n+1}OH\).

⇒  \( 12n + (1\times (2n+1)) + 16.0 + 1.0 = 60\)

= (14n +18 = 60\)

\(n = \frac{60-18}{14} = \frac{42}{14} = 3\)

Hence, the alkanol is gotten by putting n=3,

=\(C_{3}H_{7}OH\)
